key_insight: Fight World Model separates combat rules from video rendering: an executable engine decides what happens, while the visual model depicts it. This makes game logic—not visual plausibility—the authority on combat outcomes.
problem_solved: Video world models can generate convincing fights but struggle to maintain persistent state and keep hit reactions and health changes consistent with executable game rules.
method: Use an executable engine to maintain game state and resolve combat interactions.
Apply a deterministic compiler to encode engine-resolved outcomes.
Separate rule-governed combat execution from video rendering to support programmable, extensible gameplay.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, FWM offers an architecture for combining generative visuals with explicit state and rule enforcement. This could make interactive AI worlds more controllable and customizable.
visual_elements: Split pipeline diagram: combat engine → deterministic compiler → visual rendering.
Side-by-side comparison of plausible-looking combat versus rule-consistent combat.

Modular game-rule icons illustrating customizable combat mechanics.
paper_title: Fight World Model: Customizable Combat through Visual Interaction Proxies
paper_authors: Jiahua Li, Zixu John, Tom Zhong, Fuping Wu, Tianhao Xu
